key_insight: The paper turns LLM benchmarking into a multi-task statistical estimation problem, using cross-domain information to improve both domain-specific and overall scores.
engineering_relevance: It offers a more rigorous way to compare and rank LLMs across mixed benchmark suites, which is useful for leaderboard design and model selection in practice.
method: Model item-level benchmark responses with an Item Response Theory framework.
Use representation multi-task learning to share signal across domains while estimating latent LLM traits.
Derive an efficient estimator and prove minimax optimality under asymptotic settings.
evidence_signal: The approach is evaluated on MMLU leaderboard data covering 4,272 LLMs and 13,232 items across 56 subjects, with simulations showing improved performance over competing methods.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees rely on asymptotic assumptions, so finite-sample behavior and benchmark shift may affect real-world reliability.
paper_title: LLM Benchmarking via Representation Multi-task Learning
